speaker: Doctor
text: I have heard your symptoms of fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for sinusitis. To better understand your condition, can you describe the characteristics of the pain in your flank, and have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as color or frequency? Additionally, what specific antibiotics were you prescribed for your sinusitis?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain you describe sounds concerning for a kidney issue; could you tell me if the urine has changed color or if you have noticed any blood? Also, were the antibiotics you took for your sinusitis broad-spectrum, such as amoxicillin-clavulanate?

speaker: Doctor
text: Those findings of eosinophiluria alongside fever and flank pain are classic signs of an allergic interstitial nephritis. Were you taking a penicillin-based antibiotic like amoxicillin-clavulanate or cephalosporins when this started? Also, do you have a history of similar reactions to medications?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of a rash appearing on penicillin and resolving after switching to a cephalosporin strongly supports a diagnosis of Acute Interstitial Nephritis. Does the rash reappear if you ingest any other beta-lactam medications? Also, have you noticed decreased urine output or swelling in your legs recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to beta-lactam antibiotic hypersensitivity. The presence of eosinophiluria, fever, flank pain, and the specific history of rash development upon re-exposure to different beta-lactams confirms this diagnosis.
